scenes.tts: If starting size alone does not decide, what does? Is it silence, or being quieter than a neighbour?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Focal Block. Two rule cards, blank for now.
scenes.narration: If starting size alone does not decide, what does? Is it silence, or being quieter than a neighbour?

scenes.tts: In newborn rat muscle, blocking nerve impulses with tetrodotoxin slows elimination.
scenes.visual: A whole muscle with its nerve; a toxin icon blocks the nerve; a clock for elimination runs slower.
scenes.narration: In newborn rat muscle, blocking nerve impulses with tetrodotoxin slows elimination.

scenes.tts: Chronic electrical stimulation, with some patterns, speeds it up. So activity sets the pace.
scenes.visual: An electrode stimulates; the clock runs faster for some patterns, not others. Label: activity sets the pace.
scenes.narration: Chronic electrical stimulation, with some patterns, speeds it up. So activity sets the pace.

scenes.tts: But these tests changed every input at once. They could not say whether a quiet input is lost because of its neighbours. Two rules were left to separate.
scenes.visual: All inputs on a fiber dim or brighten together; the two rule cards appear.
scenes.narration: But these tests changed every input at once. They could not say whether a quiet input is lost because of its neighbours. Two rules were left to separate.

scenes.tts: Rule one. A silent synapse is removed.
scenes.visual: Rule card one: a silent synapse is removed.
scenes.narration: Rule one. A silent synapse is removed.

scenes.tts: Rule two. A synapse is removed when it is less active than nearby synapses, if enough of them are active.
scenes.visual: Rule card two: removed when less active than the synapses near it, if enough of them are active.
scenes.narration: Rule two. A synapse is removed when it is less active than nearby synapses, if enough of them are active.

scenes.tts: To tell them apart, silence part of one junction, and leave the rest working.
scenes.visual: A single endplate with one patch shaded.
scenes.narration: To tell them apart, silence part of one junction, and leave the rest working.

scenes.tts: Alpha bungarotoxin, the snake toxin from the imaging, binds acetylcholine receptors almost irreversibly. It blocks each one it binds.
scenes.caption: Alpha-bungarotoxin, the snake toxin from the imaging, binds acetylcholine receptors almost irreversibly. It blocks each one it binds.
scenes.visual: Toxin molecules settle onto receptors and stay bound.
scenes.narration: Alpha-bungarotoxin, the snake toxin from the imaging, binds acetylcholine receptors almost irreversibly. It blocks each one it binds.

scenes.tts: Where it sits, the muscle stops responding. The axon above is untouched. So quieter here means the muscle responds less.
scenes.visual: Transmitter released over the blocked receptors produces no response; the axon above still fires.
scenes.narration: Where it sits, the muscle stops responding. The axon above is untouched. So quieter here means the muscle responds less.

scenes.tts: In a living mouse, put toxin on one small patch of one endplate. At a second endplate, cover every receptor.
scenes.visual: Two endplates side by side: left, a dark wash over one small patch; right, a dark wash over the whole endplate.
scenes.narration: In a living mouse, put toxin on one small patch of one endplate. At a second endplate, cover every receptor.

scenes.tts: Predict. Over the following weeks, what does each rule say will happen at each junction?
scenes.visual: Question card between the two endplates, with the two rule cards below.
scenes.narration: Predict. Over the following weeks, what does each rule say will happen at each junction?

scenes.tts: Rule one predicts loss at both junctions. Both have silent sites.
scenes.visual: Rule card one projects loss onto both endplates.
scenes.narration: Rule one predicts loss at both junctions. Both have silent sites.

scenes.tts: Rule two predicts loss only at a partial block, where a small silent patch sits beside a larger working area.
scenes.visual: Rule card two projects loss onto the left patch only.
scenes.narration: Rule two predicts loss only at a partial block, where a small silent patch sits beside a larger working area.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-four, Rita Balice-Gordon and Lichtman reported the result.
scenes.caption: In 1994, Rita Balice-Gordon and Lichtman reported the result.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Balice-Gordon and Lichtman, 1994, living mice.
scenes.narration: In 1994, Rita Balice-Gordon and Lichtman reported the result.

scenes.tts: At the partial block, the patch lost its receptors, and the nerve terminal withdrew from it.
scenes.visual: A time bar runs weeks; on the left endplate the blocked patch empties and the terminal above it pulls back.
scenes.narration: At the partial block, the patch lost its receptors, and the nerve terminal withdrew from it.

scenes.tts: At the full block, nothing was eliminated.
scenes.visual: The right endplate stays intact. Rule card one greys out.
scenes.narration: At the full block, nothing was eliminated.

scenes.tts: At the full block, every site is equally silent. No site is quieter than its neighbour. Rule two wins.
scenes.visual: Rule card two lights up.
scenes.narration: At the full block, every site is equally silent. No site is quieter than its neighbour. Rule two wins.

scenes.tts: And the loss stayed inside the patch. The signal behind it, and how far it travels, were not identified.
scenes.visual: Arrow to the receptors, not the axon. An outline traces the patch of loss. Tag: signal and its range unknown.
scenes.narration: And the loss stayed inside the patch. The signal behind it, and how far it travels, were not identified.

scenes.tts: The amount of active territory mattered. A large active area removed a small silent one. A small active area could not.
scenes.visual: Two schematic junctions: a small blocked patch in a large active area is lost; a large blocked area beside a small active rim stays. Label: schematic.
scenes.narration: The amount of active territory mattered. A large active area removed a small silent one. A small active area could not.

scenes.tts: The loss happened where the toxin was put. So a local difference in activity directs which sites go.
scenes.visual: Two separate schematic junctions, each with a different small patch blocked; loss develops at each treated patch. Label: separate illustrative trials.
scenes.narration: The loss happened where the toxin was put. So a local difference in activity directs which sites go.

scenes.tts: Lo and Poo built the smallest contest, in cultures from the frog Zenopus.
scenes.caption: Lo and Poo built the smallest contest, in cultures from the frog Xenopus.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Lo and Poo, 1991, Xenopus culture. Three cells: two spinal neurons on one muscle cell.
scenes.narration: Lo and Poo built the smallest contest, in cultures from the frog Xenopus.

scenes.tts: Two spinal neurons shared one muscle cell. A burst to one neuron immediately weakened the other's synapse.
scenes.visual: A tetanus symbol on neuron one; the recorded response from neuron two drops.
scenes.narration: Two spinal neurons shared one muscle cell. A burst to one neuron immediately weakened the other's synapse.

scenes.tts: Predict. What if both neurons get the burst together?
scenes.visual: Both neurons get the tetanus symbol. Question card.
scenes.narration: Predict. What if both neurons get the burst together?

scenes.tts: The suppression was largely absent. Neither input was left quiet while the other was driven.
scenes.visual: Both responses hold steady. Label: activity at the same time seems to protect both.
scenes.narration: The suppression was largely absent. Neither input was left quiet while the other was driven.

scenes.tts: This is heterosynaptic depression, a weakening within minutes. It fits rule two, but it is not removal of a synapse.
scenes.visual: Label: heterosynaptic depression; functional weakening in culture, not structural removal.
scenes.narration: This is heterosynaptic depression, a weakening within minutes. It fits rule two, but it is not removal of a synapse.

scenes.tts: For two whole axons, mice had one of two inputs made weaker. The more powerful inputs were strongly favoured.
scenes.visual: Two axons of equal thickness on a fiber; one is marked reduced transmitter release and gives a smaller muscle response. Across schematic examples, the stronger input usually keeps the endplate.
scenes.narration: For two whole axons, mice had one of two inputs made weaker. The more powerful inputs were strongly favoured.

scenes.tts: Still, it is a bias, not a verdict.
scenes.visual: A tilted balance leans toward the stronger input; other weights on the pan are labelled 'other factors, unresolved'. It does not tip the same way every time.
scenes.narration: Still, it is a bias, not a verdict.

scenes.tts: What carries the message is still open. In one model, the muscle punishes inactive sites and protects the active one.
scenes.visual: Schematic labelled candidate: the muscle sends a punish arrow to a quiet terminal.
scenes.narration: What carries the message is still open. In one model, the muscle punishes inactive sites and protects the active one.

scenes.tts: Without one form of P K C, elimination in mice is delayed, but it still completes. Mice lacking B D N F or p seventy-five eliminate synapses on schedule. So none of these is yet shown to be the indispensable signal.
scenes.visual: A protect arrow to the active terminal. Tag: candidates; affecting the pace and being required are different tests.
scenes.narration: Without one form of PKC, elimination in mice is delayed, but it still completes. Mice lacking BDNF or p75 eliminate synapses on schedule. So none of these is yet shown to be the indispensable signal.
scenes.caption: Without one form of PKC, elimination in mice is delayed, but it still completes. Mice lacking BDNF or p75 eliminate synapses on schedule. So none of these is yet shown to be the indispensable signal.

scenes.tts: So silence alone does not remove a synapse. Being quieter than its neighbours puts it at risk.
scenes.visual: Closing card: silence alone does not remove a synapse; being quieter than its neighbours puts it at risk.
scenes.narration: So silence alone does not remove a synapse. Being quieter than its neighbours puts it at risk.
